idiom_name: [ThreadStatic] static field / ThreadLocal<T> with value factory
implementation_notes: The BCL carries per-thread state: `[ThreadStatic]` marks a static field as one slot per thread, and `ThreadLocal<T>` wraps lazy per-thread values with a factory (and is IDisposable). The confinement discipline is that no reference to the per-thread object escapes into a field, a callback or a Task continuation - the BCL stores only your reference, it does not stop you from publishing it. `[ThreadStatic]` field initializers run on one thread only, so every other thread reads null/0 and must initialize lazily; `ThreadLocal<T>` on a pooled thread keeps its values for the thread's lifetime, so long-lived pools should dispose the instance or the per-thread values stay alive. Use this variant when the state is genuinely thread-affine (native handles, thread-local scratch), not merely request-scoped.
pitfalls: [ThreadStatic] field initializers execute only on the first thread that touches the field; all other threads see default values, so initialization must be lazy.
ThreadLocal<T> values are only reclaimed when the owning ThreadLocal is disposed or the thread dies; with trackAllValues enabled its Values collection also keeps every thread's value alive by design.
A thread pool reuses threads indefinitely, so leftover per-thread state from one request is visible to the next unless the code resets it.

variants.name: AsyncLocal<T> (async-flow-scoped)
variants.implementation_notes: AsyncLocal<T> stores ambient data in the ExecutionContext, so the value follows an asynchronous control flow across await points and thread-pool hops instead of staying with the OS thread - the right replacement when the logical unit of work is an async operation and ThreadLocal would lose (or wrongly pin) the value. Setting Value inside a called method does not flow back to the caller, because mutation copies the context; constructor callbacks can observe context transitions. Use AsyncLocal for request, tenant and trace context; keep ThreadLocal<T> for genuinely thread-affine state.
pitfalls: AsyncLocal values flow downward from the setter: a callee's write is invisible to the caller, so two-way communication needs explicit state.
The change-notification callback runs on every execution-context transition and must be cheap and non-throwing.
Disposables stored in AsyncLocal outlive their intended scope when continuations capture the ExecutionContext; scope them explicitly or pass them as parameters.
